overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of Husserl's analyses of time, the body, and the shared world. You'll be asked about time-consciousness in terms of primal impression, retention, and protention, the lived body and kinaesthesis, and the lifeworld and intersubjectivity.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Listening to a phrase, you hear the fourth word while the third still rings as just past. How is the third word given?

options.html: It's recalled in a new act of remembering
options.text: It's recalled in a new act of remembering
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

options.html: It's retained as just past within the present
options.text: It's retained as just past within the present
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The third word is held in retention, part of the present experience and given as just past.

options.html: It's anticipated as the word about to come
options.text: It's anticipated as the word about to come
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on primal impression, retention, and protention.

options.html: It's no longer part of the experience at all
options.text: It's no longer part of the experience at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on primal impression, retention, and protention.

forms.stemHtml: Walking downstairs in the dark, your foot meets nothing where you expected a step. What does the jolt reveal?

options.html: That you had consciously predicted the number of steps
options.text: That you had consciously predicted the number of steps
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

options.html: That your experience already contained an anticipation
options.text: That your experience already contained an anticipation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The surprise reveals protention: an anticipation built into experience, which the world failed to fulfill.

options.html: That you had forgotten the number of steps from before
options.text: That you had forgotten the number of steps from before
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

options.html: That your retention of the last step was mistaken
options.text: That your retention of the last step was mistaken
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's term for the now-phase of experience, what is given as happening now? Enter two words.

options.html: primal impression
options.text: primal impression
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Primal impression is the now-phase, flanked by retention and protention.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on primal impression, retention, and protention.

forms.stemHtml: A physiotherapist measures your knee's range of motion while you feel a twinge in it. In Husserl's terms, how is your knee given?

options.html: As two knees, one measured and one felt
options.text: As two knees, one measured and one felt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

options.html: As one knee, measured as Körper and felt as Leib
options.text: As one knee, measured as Körper and felt as Leib
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The measured knee is the body as a physical thing. The felt twinge belongs to the body as lived. It's one knee, given in two ways.

options.html: As Leib to the therapist and Körper to you
options.text: As Leib to the therapist and Körper to you
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

options.html: As a mental image produced by the twinge
options.text: As a mental image produced by the twinge
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are features of the lived body (Leib)? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It is the bearer of localized sensings
options.text: It is the bearer of localized sensings
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensings are felt in the lived body itself.

options.html: It is moved immediately by the will
options.text: It is moved immediately by the will
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The lived body is the organ of the will.

options.html: It is seen from a perspective, like other things
options.text: It is seen from a perspective, like other things
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the zero point and the organ of the will.

options.html: It is first revealed through vision
options.text: It is first revealed through vision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on touch, vision, and the lived body.

forms.stemHtml: Turning your head, you feel yourself turning as the view shifts. What is Husserl's term for this felt sense of your own movement? Enter one word.

options.html: kinaesthesis
options.text: kinaesthesis
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Kinaesthesis is the felt sense of one's own movement, correlated with changes in appearance.

options.html: kinesthesis
options.text: kinesthesis
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Kinaesthesis (also spelled kinesthesis) is the felt sense of one's own movement.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on kinaesthesis and the if–then structure.

forms.stemHtml: Which claim is an example of the surreptitious substitution?

options.html: "Thermometers let us compare temperatures precisely."
options.text: "Thermometers let us compare temperatures precisely."
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

options.html: "Warmth is really just molecular motion."
options.text: "Warmth is really just molecular motion."
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The claim takes the idealized construct for the reality of warmth, forgetting that the concept was built from lived warmth.

options.html: "This room feels warmer than the hallway does."
options.text: "This room feels warmer than the hallway does."
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

options.html: "Temperature is measured on several scales."
options.text: "Temperature is measured on several scales."
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's main target in the Crisis?

options.html: The results of mathematical physics, which he thought false
options.text: The results of mathematical physics, which he thought false
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

options.html: Science's self-understanding: its idealizations taken as reality
options.text: Science's self-understanding: its idealizations taken as reality
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Husserl accepts scientific results. He criticizes the forgetting of the lifeworld that gives them meaning.

options.html: The use of experiments in the natural sciences
options.text: The use of experiments in the natural sciences
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

options.html: The influence of philosophy on scientific research
options.text: The influence of philosophy on scientific research
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

forms.stemHtml: In Husserl's account, how is another person's experience given to you?

options.html: Originally, just as your own experience is given
options.text: Originally, just as your own experience is given
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

options.html: Appresented: co-given with their body, never originally
options.text: Appresented: co-given with their body, never originally
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The other's experience is co-given along with their perceived body, but you can never have it as your own.

options.html: Only by inference from their words and actions
options.text: Only by inference from their words and actions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

options.html: Not at all, since others' minds are unknowable
options.text: Not at all, since others' minds are unknowable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are critiques commonly raised against Husserl's account of others? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: His starting point leads to solipsism
options.text: His starting point leads to solipsism
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics argue that starting from the individual subject makes others derivative.

options.html: Pairing is a disguised argument from analogy
options.text: Pairing is a disguised argument from analogy
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics read pairing as the weak inference "that body is like mine, so it has a mind."

options.html: He denies that other people's bodies can be perceived
options.text: He denies that other people's bodies can be perceived
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

options.html: He holds that we feel others' pains as our own
options.text: He holds that we feel others' pains as our own
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

forms.stemHtml: The day after a concert, you run through its opening melody in your head. How does this differ from hearing the melody's just-past notes during the concert?

options.html: It's the same act, only lasting longer than before
options.text: It's the same act, only lasting longer than before
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

options.html: It's a new act that re-presents the melody as past
options.text: It's a new act that re-presents the melody as past
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Recalling the melody is recollection, a new act. The just-past notes at the concert were retained as part of perceiving.

options.html: It's a perception, while hearing the notes was memory
options.text: It's a perception, while hearing the notes was memory
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

options.html: It's protention, reaching forward to the next note
options.text: It's protention, reaching forward to the next note
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

forms.stemHtml: What is the regress problem in Husserl's account of time?

options.html: The past grows fainter until it can no longer be recalled
options.text: The past grows fainter until it can no longer be recalled
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

options.html: If time-awareness is itself in time, another awareness is needed
options.text: If time-awareness is itself in time, another awareness is needed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If the flow must be experienced in time, a further consciousness seems needed at every level, without end.

options.html: Protention can reach no further ahead than a few seconds
options.text: Protention can reach no further ahead than a few seconds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

options.html: Each melody must be heard twice before it can be understood
options.text: Each melody must be heard twice before it can be understood
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's term for the just-past held in the present experience and given as just past? Enter one word.

options.html: retention
options.text: retention
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Retention is part of the present experience, not a separate act of memory.

options.html: recollection
options.text: recollection
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on primal impression, retention, and protention.

forms.stemHtml: When one hand touches the other and then the roles switch, what does this double sensation show?

options.html: That touch gives only the properties of physical things
options.text: That touch gives only the properties of physical things
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

options.html: That the two hands are two separate lived bodies
options.text: That the two hands are two separate lived bodies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

options.html: That each hand can be felt as touching or as touched
options.text: That each hand can be felt as touching or as touched
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The same hand shows up as a thing perceived and as a bearer of sensings, and the roles can reverse.

options.html: That vision is needed to recognize one's own hands
options.text: That vision is needed to recognize one's own hands
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following illustrate the if–then structure of perception? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: If I turn my head left, the cup's right side comes into view
options.text: If I turn my head left, the cup's right side comes into view
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A felt movement is correlated with a change in appearance.

options.html: If I step forward, the cup's profile grows larger
options.text: If I step forward, the cup's profile grows larger
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A felt movement is correlated with a change in appearance.

options.html: If the cup is red, then it reflects long wavelengths
options.text: If the cup is red, then it reflects long wavelengths
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on kinaesthesis and the if–then structure.

options.html: If I remember the cup, then it existed in the past
options.text: If I remember the cup, then it existed in the past
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on kinaesthesis and the if–then structure.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's German term for the lived body, the body as lived and sensed from within? Enter one word.

options.html: Leib
options.text: Leib
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Leib is the body as lived, in contrast to the Körper, the body as a physical thing.

options.html: Körper
options.text: Körper
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

forms.stemHtml: What does Husserl mean by the "garb of ideas"?

options.html: The historical costume of early modern scientists
options.text: The historical costume of early modern scientists
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

options.html: The lifeworld as it appears to ordinary people
options.text: The lifeworld as it appears to ordinary people
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

options.html: Science's covering of idealizations over the lifeworld
options.text: Science's covering of idealizations over the lifeworld
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The garb fits the lifeworld so closely that it's taken for the world itself.

options.html: The private images each person forms of the world
options.text: The private images each person forms of the world
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the surreptitious substitution.

forms.stemHtml: Why is the lifeworld the ground of meaning for the sciences?

options.html: Because scientists must believe in common sense over theory
options.text: Because scientists must believe in common sense over theory
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

options.html: Because concepts idealize what it gives, and tests end in it
options.text: Because concepts idealize what it gives, and tests end in it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Scientific concepts get their sense from idealizing what the lifeworld gives, and their evidence from perceptions made within it.

options.html: Because it contains the true mathematical structure of nature
options.text: Because it contains the true mathematical structure of nature
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

options.html: Because each scientist has a private lifeworld of their own
options.text: Because each scientist has a private lifeworld of their own
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Husserl say pairing isn't an argument from analogy?

options.html: Because pairing applies only to people we know well
options.text: Because pairing applies only to people we know well
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

options.html: Because pairing is a passive link, not a reasoning step
options.text: Because pairing is a passive link, not a reasoning step
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Pairing happens before any reasoning. Another body similar to one's own is immediately apprehended as lived.

options.html: Because pairing relies on scientific evidence about bodies
options.text: Because pairing relies on scientific evidence about bodies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

options.html: Because pairing is a conscious guess we can revise freely
options.text: Because pairing is a conscious guess we can revise freely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are defenders' replies to critiques of Husserl's account of others? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Pairing is passive, not an inference
options.text: Pairing is passive, not an inference
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Because pairing isn't a reasoning step, the analogy objection misses its target.

options.html: Openness to others is built into experience
options.text: Openness to others is built into experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Every perceived thing is given as perceivable by others too.

options.html: Others' experiences are given to us originally
options.text: Others' experiences are given to us originally
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

options.html: Only one's own mind can be known to exist
options.text: Only one's own mind can be known to exist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

forms.stemHtml: Husserl calls retention "primary memory." Why isn't retention simply a short memory?

options.html: Because it concerns only the most recent second of sound
options.text: Because it concerns only the most recent second of sound
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

options.html: Because it's stored in a different part of the brain
options.text: Because it's stored in a different part of the brain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

options.html: Because it's a phase of perception, not a re-presenting act
options.text: Because it's a phase of perception, not a re-presenting act
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Memory is a separate act that re-presents the past. Retention is a phase of the present perception that gives the just-past as itself.

options.html: Because it applies only to melodies and not to speech
options.text: Because it applies only to melodies and not to speech
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention vs. recollection.

forms.stemHtml: How does James's specious present differ from Husserl's account of the present?

options.html: James denies that the experienced present has any breadth
options.text: James denies that the experienced present has any breadth
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on James's specious present and current research.

options.html: Husserl treats the present as a durationless instant
options.text: Husserl treats the present as a durationless instant
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on James's specious present and current research.

options.html: James describes a span; Husserl describes a structure
options.text: James describes a span; Husserl describes a structure
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both agree the present has breadth. James treats it as a short span of time. Husserl describes a structure of primal impression, retention, and protention.

options.html: James studies memory, while Husserl studies perception
options.text: James studies memory, while Husserl studies perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on James's specious present and current research.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's term for the open anticipation, within the present experience, of what is about to come? Enter one word.

options.html: protention
options.text: protention
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Protention is built into experience and is most visible when it fails, as in surprise.

options.html: prediction
options.text: prediction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on protention, surprise, and the regress problem.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on primal impression, retention, and protention.

forms.stemHtml: What does it mean to call the lived body the zero point of orientation?

options.html: The body has no weight when it's felt from within
options.text: The body has no weight when it's felt from within
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the zero point and the organ of the will.

options.html: The body is the absolute "here" from which all is "there"
options.text: The body is the absolute "here" from which all is "there"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Wherever you go, your body is "here," and everything else is given as "there" relative to it.

options.html: The body is located at the center of any room
options.text: The body is located at the center of any room
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the zero point and the organ of the will.

options.html: The body is the point at which perception begins in time
options.text: The body is the point at which perception begins in time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the zero point and the organ of the will.

forms.stemHtml: Why does touch, not vision, first give the body as lived, on Husserl's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Touch localizes sensings in the body itself
options.text: Touch localizes sensings in the body itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When one hand touches the other, sensings are felt in it.

options.html: The eye doesn't see itself or its own sensations
options.text: The eye doesn't see itself or its own sensations
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Visual sensations aren't localized in the eye, so vision presents the body only as a thing.

options.html: Touch gives more accurate information about objects
options.text: Touch gives more accurate information about objects
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on touch, vision, and the lived body.

options.html: Vision works only for objects far away from the body
options.text: Vision works only for objects far away from the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on touch, vision, and the lived body.

forms.stemHtml: What is the English term (Rojcewicz and Schuwer) for Husserl's Empfindnisse, sensations localized in the lived body? Enter one word.

options.html: sensings
options.text: sensings
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensings are felt in the lived body itself, as opposed to properties of the object touched.

options.html: sensing
options.text: sensing
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensings are felt in the lived body itself, as opposed to properties of the object touched.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Leib and Körper.

forms.stemHtml: How did Galileo's mathematization treat the shapes of perceived bodies?

options.html: It left perceived shapes exactly as they are given
options.text: It left perceived shapes exactly as they are given
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

options.html: It idealized them into exact geometric limit-shapes
options.text: It idealized them into exact geometric limit-shapes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Perceived, more-or-less shapes were replaced by idealities such as perfect circles, which no perceived body exactly has.

options.html: It treated them as indirectly measurable qualities
options.text: It treated them as indirectly measurable qualities
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

options.html: It dismissed them as illusions of the senses
options.text: It dismissed them as illusions of the senses
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Husserl's Crisis and Galileo's mathematization.

forms.stemHtml: Which description fits the lifeworld?

options.html: The idealized world described by mathematical laws
options.text: The idealized world described by mathematical laws
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

options.html: A private world of each person's sensations
options.text: A private world of each person's sensations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

options.html: The worldview of people before modern science
options.text: The worldview of people before modern science
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the garb of ideas and the lifeworld.

options.html: The pregiven, prescientific world shared with others
options.text: The pregiven, prescientific world shared with others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The lifeworld is always already given, precedes and grounds science, and is shared, including by scientists today.

forms.stemHtml: For Husserl, what makes the world objective?

options.html: Its existing with no one there to perceive it
options.text: Its existing with no one there to perceive it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

options.html: Its being the same for all possible perceivers
options.text: Its being the same for all possible perceivers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Objectivity depends on intersubjectivity. A world is objective because it's there for everyone, not for no one.

options.html: Its being described in exact mathematical terms
options.text: Its being described in exact mathematical terms
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

options.html: Its being certain to one subject beyond all doubt
options.text: Its being certain to one subject beyond all doubt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on intersubjectivity, objectivity, and critiques.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following belong to Husserl's account of how others are given? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Pairing, a passive link with one's own lived body
options.text: Pairing, a passive link with one's own lived body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Pairing apprehends another similar body as lived.

options.html: Appresentation of the other's experience with their body
options.text: Appresentation of the other's experience with their body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The other's experience is co-given, but never originally.

options.html: Direct perception of the other's thoughts and feelings
options.text: Direct perception of the other's thoughts and feelings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.

options.html: Inference from brain scans to mental states
options.text: Inference from brain scans to mental states
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on empathy, pairing, and appresentation.
